issues.description: The template implementation of make_y_state is missing the depolarization probability parameter p in its signature, but the problem statement and the solution both specify make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. This will cause a parameter mismatch (TypeError) when tests or student code call make_y_state with the p argument and prevents students from following the intended design for injecting noisy |Y> states.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the p parameter to match the specification and solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update the function's docstring to document the p parameter and ensure any internal usage matches the intended noisy |Y> preparation.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define make_y_state to accept a depolarization strength parameter named 'p' (make_y_state(circ, q, p)), but the template implementation declares make_y_state(circ, q) with no 'p' parameter. This mismatch in the function signature for the same conceptual operation (preparing a noisy |Y> state with depolarization probability p) can confuse students about how to implement and call the function and whether noise strength should be provided.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's make_y_state signature to include the depolarization parameter 'p' (def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None) and update the docstring accordingly so it matches the problem statement and solution.
